title.en: Explain how statistics helps economic policy

say.en: Before fixing the minimum support price for ragi, the government looks at costs of cultivation from thousands of farms. Why not just guess? In this lesson: List the functions of statistics.
Explain how statistics helps economic policy.

body.en: *Statistics* presents economic facts in a precise and definite form, condenses a mass of data into a few numbers such as averages and percentages, and helps compare and find relationships between economic factors, such as price and demand.
body.kn: ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಸಂಗತಿಗಳನ್ನು ನಿಖರವಾಗಿ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ದೊಡ್ಡ ದತ್ತಾಂಶವನ್ನು ಸರಾಸರಿ, ಶೇಕಡಾವಾರು ರೂಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಕ್ಷಿಪ್ತಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಬಂಧಗಳನ್ನು ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: What statistics does for economics

say.en: A long list of marks tells us little. Statistics condenses it into one number, the average.
Percentages let us compare: this year 80% passed, last year 72%.
Statistics also shows relationships, such as price and quantity demanded.
Governments use these numbers to plan and to check whether policies worked.

How the quantity demanded changes when price changes
Estimating next year's demand for electricity
Using price data to decide support prices for farmers

explanation.en: Statistics turns a mass of economic facts into precise, condensed and comparable figures that help test theories, forecast and frame policy.

say.en: Why economics needs statistics Match each use of statistics with an example.

body.en: Economists use data to test economic theories and to forecast. Governments use *statistics* to plan, to frame policies on prices, employment and poverty, and to check whether those policies worked.
body.kn: ಅರ್ಥಶಾಸ್ತ್ರಜ್ಞರು ಸಿದ್ಧಾಂತ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಲು ಮತ್ತು ಮುನ್ಸೂಚನೆಗೆ ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ಬಳಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಯೋಜನೆ, ನೀತಿ ರೂಪಿಸುವಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನಕ್ಕೆ ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: The marks of 60 students in economics are given in a long list. Name two ways statistics can make this list meaningful to the principal.

steps.en: Condense: find the average mark of the class.
Compare: find the percentage of students who passed, and compare it with last year.

answer.en: Find an average (condensation) and a pass percentage for comparison
